chunks.text: 66-year-old male, Senior Official or Manager, resident of Tampines, Singapore.
Right ulna fracture healed 20 years ago
Peptic ulcer disease resolved 10 years ago
Spinal anesthesia with bupivacaine and fentanyl, supplemented with propofol sedation
General anesthesia for cholecystectomy 15 years ago, no complications

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr Tan. I'm Dr Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you today. Let me go through some questions to make sure we're all set for your hernia surgery. First, can you tell me a bit about your hernia and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doc. This hernia on my left side has been bulging for almost a year now. It doesn't hurt much, but my surgeon said it's better to fix it before it gets worse. I had a similar one on the right side done ten years back, no problems then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's talk about your medications. I see you're on quite a few. Can you list them out for me, including doses and how often you take them?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I take amlodipine 10mg every morning for blood pressure, metoprolol 50mg twice daily for my heart rhythm, metformin 500mg three times a day for diabetes, glimepiride 4mg daily, atorvastatin 20mg at night, digoxin 0.125mg daily, and warfarin 5mg every evening. Oh, and enalapril... wait, I stopped that one already.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You mentioned enalapril. The records show it's still active, but you stopped it? Can you tell me when and why you discontinued it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah yes, doc. I stopped enalapril about six months ago because of this terrible dry cough that wouldn't go away. My GP said it's a common side effect, so we switched me to amlodipine instead. I forgot to update the hospital records properly, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Any known allergies to medications or other substances?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin. Got a bad rash the one time I took it as a young man. Never touched it since.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Have you fasted as instructed before surgery? Nothing by mouth after midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doc. I had my last sip of water at 6am. My wife made sure I didn't sneak any breakfast, haha!

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. You mentioned a previous hernia surgery. Did you have any anesthesia complications then?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No issues at all. They gave me spinal anesthesia too, and I was awake but sleepy through it. Recovered fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. How about your overall fitness? Can you walk up a flight of stairs without getting short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can manage 2-3 flights slowly, but I do get a bit winded. My diabetes and heart condition slow me down a little, but I'm still independent with daily activities.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for all that information. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia using bupivacaine and fentanyl, plus some propofol to keep you relaxed. Your blood pressure medications and warfarin management have been reviewed with the surgical team. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doc. Just want to get this done and recover smoothly. Thanks for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] spinal anesthesia administered bupivacaine two point five milligrams and fentanyl twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] eighteen gauge IV catheter placed in left antecubital fossa

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] blood pressure eighty over fifty, ephedrine ten milligrams IV given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] normal saline bolus one thousand milliliters administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] propofol infusion started at fifty micrograms per kilogram per minute

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] blood pressure one hundred fifty over ninety, labetalol ten milligrams IV given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:35] maintenance fluids at one hundred milliliters per hour started

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] patient breathing spontaneously, oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent on nasal cannula

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Quite okay, Doctor. Got some pain at the operation site, but manageable lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Can you rate your pain on a scale of 0 to 10 for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 3 or 4? Not too bad, but I can feel it when I move.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. Any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no vomiting. Stomach feels a bit funny, but I think it's okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Breathing comfortably? Any chest tightness or shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. No problem with chest, thank God.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Did you experience any awareness or discomfort during the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. Slept like a baby, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Any issues with your blood pressure, sugar levels, or heart palpitations?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Blood pressure was a bit high before surgery, but nurses said it's stable now. Sugar was 12 this morning, but I took my medicine. No dizziness or fast heart beats.
